Thursday, July l8, at 11:15
o'clock, Miss Janis Brown became
the bride of Howard Devol, Jr.,
at a beautiful double ring cere-
mony performed at Newport, KY,
by Rev. J. E. Smith.


The bride chose for her wedding
a powder blue gabardine suit with
accessories of black and white. Her
corsage was of gardenias.


The couple were attended by Mr..
and Mrs. James Carter. Mrs. Carter
wore a gray dress with white and
tan accessories. Her corsage was
of gardenias also.


Mrs. Devol is the only daughter
of Mr. and Mrs. Guy Brown of
Caldwell, and was graduated from
the Caldwell high school with the
class of 1916.


Mr. Devol is the son of Howard
Devol, Sr., of South Olive, and is
a graduate of Dexter City high
school. He served more than three
years in the armed forces and
spent several months overseas. He
is employed with the Clymer Oil
Company of Dexter City.


Mr.. and Mrs. Devol will reside at
the home of the brides parents, Mr.
and Mrs. Guy Brown.

The surprising thing about the poll of service men being conducted by the Town of West Hartford to obtain views on a proposed war memorial is the small number of veterans who want to see monu- ment erected. The vast majority expressed themselves as being in favor of some sort of living mem- orial,' and only eleven of the eighty queried suggested monument. An even dozen favored scholarships or fellowships, and many favored some kind of community building.

 It would seem that if this small cross section is representative ser- vice men are more interested in something useful than in merely adding another bit of sculpture to the community. Monuments created by fine artists and planned with excellent taste, such as the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, can be almost aWesome in their beauty Unfortunately, however, there are few communities that do not still possess a monument or two, per- haps a statesman with Napoleonic stance, or a bewhiskered general on horseback. Service men were probably mindful of these when they told West Hartford authorities that they wanted a living memorial. In any event it is an uncommonly sensible thing that is being done in conducting this poll to find out what the veteran himself thinks about war memorials.
